rationale: Closes the last unexercised item of the liveness question: the executor's timeout path is now driven for real (its goroutine runs, the blocked row accumulates the grace period and the instance arrives on the recovery channel). The local construction run reports enqueued true for instance 1.0 after about 12.6 seconds, which both establishes the alternative progress path C7 relies on and measures the delay a stalled row incurs. New obligation and binding; the trusted runner and a fresh correspondence review decide the formal outcome, expected to hold.

candidate.rationale: The obligation and binding are supplied with the check so the claim exists before the plan references it; the duty is the executor's own enqueue of a blocked instance, which is the progress path relied on by the dead rejection-branch finding.

question.question: With one row blocked at an instance whose record the replica holds but which has no commands and no commit, does the executor enqueue that instance for recovery after its grace period, and roughly how long does that take in wall-clock terms?
question.importance: This is the path that lets a replica which missed an instance make progress without any client stimulus, and it is the alternative the dead rejection-path finding (C7) relies on: without the enqueue, a rejected accept round would block the row indefinitely. Establishing it as a protection also measures the delay a stalled row actually incurs.
contexts: row blocked at instance 0 by a record with no commands and no commit
executor goroutine running as in the launched configuration
event_paths: executeCommands finds the blocked instance at the head of the row
the per-row timeout counter accumulates the grace period
the suffix is pushed into instancesToRecover

counterevidence: scoped to the source: the loop breaks at the first instance it cannot apply and, when the row's counter reaches COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD, pushes every instance from the blocked one to crtInstance into instancesToRecover (S4-execute-loop)

scoped to the run: the local construction run reports the prerequisite (status 0, no commands, crtInstance 0, ExecedUpTo -1) and then enqueued true for instance 1.0 after a wait of about 12.6 seconds, which is the built-in one-millisecond-per-iteration counter reaching its limit

question.trigger_rationale: The principal fact is the per-instance record the replica holds (F1), which the blocking condition is defined against; B9-recovery-trigger consumes it when the row stalls. This is the A2 recovery relationship seen from the executor: the enqueue is what hands a blocked instance to the recovery entry, and it is the progress path that the dead rejection branch (C7) depends on.

obligation.description: When a replica's executor finds an instance it cannot apply (no commands, not committed) at the head of a row, it must enqueue that instance for recovery once the configured grace period has elapsed, so the row does not stay blocked on that replica.

scope.description: One replica whose row 1 is blocked at instance 0 by a record with no commands and no commit, with the executor goroutine running as in the launched configuration.
assumptions: crtInstance for the row is at the blocked instance and the executed watermark is behind it
no other instance in the row is ready to apply
excluded: what the recovery that follows does with the instance (other claims cover the resolution and its consequences)
the client-visible effect of the delay

grounding.derivation: executeCommands breaks out of a row at the first instance it cannot apply, accumulates the grace period in that row's timeout counter and, when the counter reaches COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD, pushes the whole suffix from the blocked instance into instancesToRecover. This is the path that lets a replica that missed an instance make progress without a client stimulus, so the duty is that the enqueue happens, not that recovery succeeds.
grounding.applicability: Applies to any replica whose executor is running with a blocked row head; the launched configuration starts executeCommands whenever Exec is true.
unresolved: the grace period is measured in loop iterations of one millisecond each in this implementation, so the wall-clock wait is an observation rather than a specification

associations.rationale: The branch that enqueues the suffix is the mechanism the claim asserts; the enqueued instance is what startRecoveryForInstance later consumes.

bindings.description: Executor loop and its per-row timeout: a blocked instance accumulates the grace period and is enqueued to instancesToRecover when it elapses.
